result:
I'd make curiosity and evidence-based reasoning the default human instinct—stronger than tribal loyalty, status-seeking, or short-term comfort.

Most of the world's persistent problems (conflict, poverty traps, environmental damage, stalled progress in health and knowledge) aren't mainly shortages of resources or technology. They're failures of coordination and epistemology: people and institutions repeatedly choose beliefs and actions that feel good or signal allegiance over ones that actually work. If the pull toward "what is true and what helps" reliably outweighed the pull toward "what my group believes" or "what flatters me," a huge fraction of those failures would shrink on their own. Science, institutions, and everyday decisions would improve faster because the feedback loops would be tighter.

Everything else—peace, prosperity, health, exploration—follows more readily once that bias is flipped. It's the highest-leverage single change I can imagine.
